Yes. After rechecking the latest implementation plan, the Living Technical Note and the current Linear inventory, this is the right setup.

The eight threads cover every core implementation issue exactly once, while the planning issues sit in the decisions thread. The completed board issue, epic rollups, conditional work and deferred work do not need dedicated discussion threads.

I would make these small refinements to the earlier names:

| Thread | Linear issues |
|---|---|
| `00-project-decisions-and-upstream` | LOD-5, LOD-6 |
| `01-local-environment-and-kurtosis` | LOD-8, LOD-24 |
| `02-builder-cli-signing-and-bn-client` | LOD-9, LOD-10, LOD-11, LOD-12 |
| `03-bn-api-payload-and-cache` | LOD-15, LOD-14, LOD-13, LOD-16 |
| `04-bid-selection-and-reveal` | LOD-17, LOD-18, LOD-19 |
| `05-protocol-outcomes-data-and-recovery` | LOD-20, LOD-21, LOD-22 |
| `06-testing-deathstar-and-security` | LOD-23, LOD-26 |
| `07-integration-devnet-and-handoff` | LOD-25, LOD-27 |

A few operating rules will prevent duplication:

- The latest implementation plan is the source of truth. The Living Technical Note is supporting research until it is updated.
- Use thread `00` for cross-cutting decisions and upstream announcements, not every technical discussion.
- Discuss implementation in the relevant technical thread, then link the final decision back into thread `00` if it affects the wider plan.
- Keep Linear as the status, ownership and dependency tracker. Keep GitHub as the code and review record.
- Create a temporary issue-specific thread only when something needs substantial maintainer input or focused PR review.
- Do not create extension threads yet. Create one only when an extension package is activated.
- Some later threads may auto-archive while inactive. That is fine. Keep an index in the parent channel so they remain easy to find.

There is no missing permanent thread for observability, registration, specifications or PR reviews. Core observability belongs with its implementation and QA work. Registration and top-ups are outside the sidecar. Specifications belong in thread `00`. PR-specific discussion can use temporary threads.

## Optional parent-channel message

```text
Marko and I are splitting the Builder work into a small set of threads so implementation discussions are easier to follow.

We will use Linear for issue status, ownership and dependencies, GitHub for code and review, and these threads for design and implementation discussion.

Latest implementation plan:
https://github.com/krisoshea-eth/lodestar-eip-7732-builder-docs/pull/2

Linear project:
https://linear.app/kriso/project/lodestar-eip-7732-builder-814d6faca6fd

The implementation plan is the current source of truth. The Living Technical Note is still useful background, but parts of it need to be brought up to date.

If a discussion affects more than one workstream, we will link the final decision in the project decisions and upstream thread as well.
```

## Copy-ready thread openers

### `00-project-decisions-and-upstream`

```text
Using this thread for decisions and upstream changes that can affect the overall Builder plan. This includes final questions for the Lodestar team, baseline or specification changes, API changes, and anything that affects more than one workstream.

Linear: LOD-5 (PLAN-01) and LOD-6 (BASELINE-01).

Technical implementation should stay in the relevant workstream thread. Once something is agreed here or elsewhere, we will update Linear and the implementation plan so the decision does not live only in Discord.
```

### `01-local-environment-and-kurtosis`

```text
Using this thread for the local Builder environment and repeatable happy-path harness. This includes the pinned Kurtosis and Gloas configuration, active Builder fixtures, deterministic proposer selection, BN and EL readiness, and the first clean bid to selection to reveal to FULL run.

Linear: LOD-8 (ENV-01) and LOD-24 (E2E-01).

Buildoor belongs here when we are using it as fixture or setup reference. The later Lodestar Builder and buildoor coexistence work belongs in the integration thread.
```

### `02-builder-cli-signing-and-bn-client`

```text
Using this thread for the standalone Builder sidecar foundation. This covers packages/builder, the lodestar builder command, configuration, local keystore and signing, readiness and shutdown, the typed source-BN client, active Builder resolution, SSE consumption and fork-correct block retrieval.

Linear: LOD-9 (CLI-01), LOD-10 (SIGN-01), LOD-11 (API-01) and LOD-12 (API-02).

BN-side route or payload-production changes should go in the BN API, payload and cache thread.
```

### `03-bn-api-payload-and-cache`

```text
Using this thread for the source-BN changes needed by the sidecar. This includes the preparation and candidate API shape, prepareNextSlot integration, Builder execution fee-recipient transport, canonical payload production, bid construction, coverability checks and reuse of the BN stateful reveal cache.

Linear: LOD-15 (BN-01), LOD-14 (BN-02), LOD-13 (BN-03) and LOD-16 (BN-04).

The sidecar consumes this surface, but the BN remains authoritative for payload construction, value, balance validation and reveal material.
```

### `04-bid-selection-and-reveal`

```text
Using this thread for the live Builder lifecycle after a candidate is available. This covers head-compatible bid requests, configurable publication timing, bid signing and publication, exact selected-bid detection, envelope retrieval, signing and immediate publication with consensus_and_equivocation validation.

Linear: LOD-17 (BID-01), LOD-18 (SELECT-01) and LOD-19 (REV-01).

Detailed BN cache implementation stays in the BN API, payload and cache thread. Deathstar proof and broader failure coverage stay in the testing and security thread.
```

### `05-protocol-outcomes-data-and-recovery`

```text
Using this thread for the evidence and recovery work that makes the local Builder loop protocol-complete. This includes PTC observations, trustless payment and accounting, non-zero blobs and data columns, and bounded recovery when only the sidecar restarts and the same source BN still has the reveal material.

Linear: LOD-20 (OUT-01), LOD-21 (DATA-01) and LOD-22 (REL-01).

This does not include multi-BN failover, durable Builder recovery or full high availability, which remain deferred.
```

### `06-testing-deathstar-and-security`

```text
Using this thread for cross-cutting failure coverage, Deathstar scenarios and the final security and resource review. This includes operator diagnostics, fail-closed cases, proposer-equivocation rejection, the PR 9757 test, key and secret handling, request bounds, payload-job concurrency and cache resource limits.

Linear: LOD-23 (QA-01) and LOD-26 (SEC-01).

Feature-specific unit tests can stay with their implementation threads. Use this thread when the test crosses components, proves a security property or needs a dedicated adversarial setup.
```

### `07-integration-devnet-and-handoff`

```text
Using this thread for broader integration and delivery after the local core loop is stable. This includes ethereum-package support, Lodestar Builder and buildoor coexistence, devnet readiness, runbooks, documentation, PR shaping, EPF outputs and maintainer handoff.

Linear: LOD-25 (INT-01) and LOD-27 (HANDOFF-01).

Conditional extensions are not active yet. If one is selected later, we will create a separate thread for that package rather than mixing it into the core work.
```

## Settled architecture and protocol decisions

- Builder deposit request type is `0x03`; Builder withdrawal credentials use prefix `0xB0`. Devnet-7 uses deposit contract `0x0000bff46984e3725691fa540a8c7589300d8282` and exit contract `0x000064d678505ad48f8ccb093bc65613800e8282`.
- Builder lifecycle currently includes a 64-request deposit cap, 64-epoch minimum withdrawability delay, payload-builder eligibility, and a system-call contract-disable path with reduced throughput limits.
- `PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS=5000`, placing the payload-availability deadline six seconds into a 12-second slot.
- [Consensus #5497](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5497) admits and propagates multiple bids compatible with the node's local head view, including relevant FULL/EMPTY paths; incompatible-branch bids are ignored.
- [Consensus #5473](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5473) looks up payload availability at the parent block slot, preventing skipped-slot timely-head errors.
- [Consensus #5495](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5495) returns early for an already-known block, preserving PTC votes and timeliness state on redelivery.
- Proposer-preference APIs are merged; invalid preferences are ignored. Dependent-root age/boundary-child rules are settled upstream and implemented by Lodestar [#9695](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9695).
- One signed execution payload envelope supports stateful and stateless publication shapes via `Eth-Blob-Data-Included`; `consensus_and_equivocation` remains the Builder-facing validation target.
- `head_v2` EMPTY→FULL second emission is a SHOULD; other FULL/EMPTY edge emissions remain implementation-specific.
- ProduceBlockV4 carries execution value for multi-beacon-node selection. Local building remains the floor, local wins ties, and remote policy uses matched/unmatched preference rules in the still-open API work.
- Lodestar forwards a bid only when it exceeds the tuple's high bid by `min(max(0.0001 ETH, 3%), 0.01 ETH)`; local acceptance and gossip forwarding are intentionally distinct.
- Bid fields that contribute to SSZ roots must remain exact `uint64` values through parsing, caching, signing, hashing, proposer preferences, `PayloadAttributesV4`, and events. Lodestar [#9749](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9749), [#9750](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9750), and [#9751](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9751) implement this on unstable; JavaScript `number` is unsafe for unbounded values above `2^53`.

"material scope or sequencing change" .-> PLAN +``` + +## Lodestar team discussion + +### Round one: architecture and workflow + +The first round of discussion settled most of the large architecture questions carried over from the Week 5 update. + +The Builder itself is a standalone `lodestar builder` process in `packages/builder`, wired into the Lodestar CLI alongside `beacon` and `validator`. It is designed to sit beside a compatible beacon node and consume standard Beacon APIs and SSE events where those surfaces are sufficient, with narrow Lodestar-specific routes or events added where the workflow genuinely needs them and useful additions proposed upstream afterwards. + +The source beacon node remains authoritative for the Engine API connection, proposer context and preferences, payload construction, Builder state, solvency checks, and reveal material; the sidecar never talks to the execution client directly. Builder onboarding is outside the first implementation's scope. The sidecar will initially import one Builder BLS key and read the active Builder's status through the [builders API](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9593), while deposits, exits, and top-ups remain external through genesis configuration or ethPandaOps tooling. + +The proposer's `target_gas_limit` flows through proposer preferences and reaches the EL through payload attributes ([execution-apis #796](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/796)). Bid selection stays a proposer-beacon-node decision; for the local test path, Lodestar can be configured to prefer the external bid with `--builder.selection builderalways`. The Builder learns that it won through beacon-node events and block retrieval rather than joining libp2p directly. + +### Round two: simplifying the first iteration + +The second round covered bid value, solvency, the trust boundary, the reveal cache, key scope, equivocation, and completion evidence. Most of the answers made the first implementation smaller. + +NC initially suggested starting the bid at 90% of execution rewards. However, Nico suggested that we set `bid.value` to the local execution-payload value behind a small strategy function, with `execution_payment = 0` for the trustless p2p bid. + +For now, builder solvency will be determined by the beacon node. The BN rejects a bid the Builder cannot cover, while the sidecar surfaces that as a clear operator warning and can expose the current balance returned by the status lookup it already needs for Builder-index resolution. + +The reveal path reuses the beacon node's stateful block-production cache model. The source BN retains the exact payload, execution requests, blobs, and proofs until reveal or bounded expiry, then evicts the material after a successful reveal. Publication validation, including any equivocation check available on the pinned baseline, stays with the beacon node. If the full upstream check is still missing when we pin, that becomes a documented upstream gap rather than a new Builder-side policy or a blocker for the first happy path. One local keystore-backed Builder key is enough for the first iteration. + +The accepted directions, condensed: + +| Area | Accepted direction | +|---|---| +| Base and workflow | Pin `unstable`; keep one shared feature branch current with it; split later when review benefits | +| Product form | Standalone `lodestar builder` command in `packages/builder`, parallel to `packages/validator`, wired into the CLI | +| EL and payload state | Source BN owns the Engine API and payload-building state; no sidecar-to-EL path | +| API boundary | Standard Beacon APIs and SSE where possible; narrow Lodestar-specific routes and events where required | +| Onboarding | Outside the first implementation — import one Builder key and read status through the builders API; deposits, exits, and top-ups remain external | +| Proposer inputs | `target_gas_limit` flows through proposer preferences and payload attributes; test selection stays BN-controlled | +| Keys | One local keystore-backed Builder key; record any missing upstream check as a gap | +| Testing | Kurtosis first; extend ethereum-package as needed using buildoor's participant configuration as a reference; devnets later | + +This planning process allowed us to define a clear ownership boundary too: + +```text +lodestar builder + owns keys, signatures, orchestration, exact matching and diagnostics + +source Lodestar beacon node + owns chain state, proposer preferences, EL access, payload construction, + solvency checks, stateful reveal material and publication validation +``` + +## The plan + +The plan is the execution document for the remainder of the fellowship. The audit is complete. There are a few final updates, but no new architecture questions for the Lodestar team.

## Important: do not sync HackMD yet

The public HackMD implementation plan is behind GitHub and contains several joined or truncated Markdown fragments. Do not push that HackMD version to GitHub.

I found no unique current section or decision in HackMD that needs to be rescued into GitHub. GitHub is the correct source of truth.

The safe order is:

1. Review and merge the local follow-up changes listed below.
2. Save/download a backup of each current HackMD note.
3. Pull `main` from GitHub into HackMD.
4. Check both source and preview modes.

## How gates and epics should work in Linear

They should remain separate dimensions:

- Epics describe workstreams.
- Gates describe delivery checkpoints.
- Cycles describe what you are doing this week.
- Leaf issues contain the actual implementation work and estimates.

For example, `BID-01` belongs under Epic C because it is Builder bid behavior, but it belongs to Gate B because a working real bid path is required to pass Gate B. That cross-cutting relationship is correct.

Your current mapping is:

| Gate | Actual deliverables |
|---|---|
| Gate 0 | PLAN-01, BASELINE-01, BOARD-01 |
| Gate A | ENV-01, CLI-01, SIGN-01, API-01, API-02 |
| Gate B | BN-01 through BN-04, BID-01 |
| Gate C | SELECT-01, REV-01, E2E-01 |
| Gate D | OUT-01, DATA-01, REL-01, QA-01 |
| Gate E | INT-01 |
| Extension decision | EXT-DEVNET-01 through EXT-UI-01 |
| Gate F | SEC-01, HANDOFF-01 |

I recommend two Linear cleanups:

1. Remove Epics A through D themselves from milestones. Only their child deliverables should count toward gate progress. Otherwise the parent epic becomes an extra issue in the milestone and slightly distorts completion percentages.

2. Remove Epic A from Cycle 2. Cycles should contain executable child issues only. Putting both an epic and its children in a cycle inflates the cycle issue count and capacity.

Use epic status like this:

- Backlog until the workstream starts.
- In Progress when its first child begins.
- Done when all required children are Done.
- No estimate on the epic itself.
- No cycle assignment on the epic.

Linear has a useful parent automation for this. In Team settings, enable:

- `Parent auto-close`: on
- `Sub-issue auto-close`: off

That lets an epic close when all children finish, while preventing someone from accidentally closing all unfinished children by marking the parent Done. [Linear parent and sub-issues](https://linear.app/docs/parent-and-sub-issues)
